samples.summary: Design doc claims the offline-copy recovery reuses the copy engine; the implementation uses the import engine instead
samples.evidence: The doc's "Losing work anyway" section says "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and the See Also list names "[document-copy.md](document-copy.md) — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts` reuses neither: it calls `createDocument()` plus `applyImportedContent()` (the Miro/upload import path) and, for notes, a bespoke Yorkie client. The choice is defensible — `POST /documents/:id/copy` copies a *server-side* document and the source here is local bytes, so the copy endpoint literally cannot serve it — but the design doc now documents a reuse relationship that does not exist, and `document-copy.md` is cited as a dependency it is not. Either the doc should name `apply-imported-content.ts` as the engine reused, or the discrepancy should be recorded.

samples.summary: `writeNote` duplicates `applyImportedContent`'s Yorkie client lifecycle instead of adding a `note` branch to it
samples.evidence: `applyImportedContent` (packages/frontend/src/app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:228) already owns the create-client / activate / attach-with-initialRoot / write / detach / deactivate lifecycle for sheet, doc, slides and board, and its own comment states the per-type root writes are "intentionally kept in step with the editor mount paths they mirror". `writeNote` re-implements that exact lifecycle verbatim (including the same 'activate() outside the try' reasoning, copied as a comment) for a fifth type, in a different file. The recovery path's note write will now not receive lifecycle fixes made to the shared engine, and the fifth type's mirror lives away from the four it is supposed to stay in step with. A `note` case on `ImportedContent` would have kept all five in one place.

samples.summary: `documentIdOf` re-implements the exported `documentKeyOf`, which this change's own comment warns against duplicating
samples.evidence: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts:212` exports `documentKeyOf(key)` (split on `/`, take last segment) and its doc comment says: "Defined here because this module is where store keys are consumed, and two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false." `durable-session.ts:1` correctly imports it. But `offline-copy.ts:52-55` defines a private `documentIdOf` doing exactly the same split, and `offline-copy-recovery.ts:146` inlines the same split a third time inside `describeArchivedDocument`. Three copies of a rule the change itself documents as having previously drifted into a silent bug. They agree today, which is why this is minor rather than major.

samples.summary: The design doc's stated offline-transition toast wording for the durable case is not implemented
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § What the user sees states: "Two consequences follow automatically: the `beforeunload` guard is suppressed when `durable`, and the offline-transition toast changes from 'keep this tab open' to 'saved to this device'." The unload-guard half is implemented (`stranded` is false in `saved-locally`, so `mayHaveUnsent` is false). The toast half is not: the toast effect is gated entirely on `stranded`, so a durable document that goes offline produces *no* toast rather than a reworded one. Arguably silence is the better product decision, but it is a different decision from the one the doc specifies, and the doc was written/updated in this same change.
searchedFor: checked sync-status-tooltip.ts for a saved-locally toast path

samples.summary: Housekeeping and purge paths are not gated on `supportsClientKey()` or the preference, contradicting "users who never opt in pay nothing"
samples.evidence: The design doc states: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing." Both opt-in entry points are correctly gated on `supportsClientKey()` (settings/page.tsx:111, sync-status-chip.tsx:85), but the housekeeping is not. `OfflineRuntime` mounts for every signed-in user from `PrivateRoute` and unconditionally constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (creating the IndexedDB database), runs `retryPendingOfflineErase`, `collectStale`, `listRecoverableWork`, and issues an extra `fetchDocuments()` per session for the reconcile. `deleteWorkspace` (api/workspaces.ts) additionally issues `fetchWorkspace()` + `fetchDocuments()` on every workspace delete, and `purgeOfflineDocuments` opens a database on every document delete. On the shipped `@yorkie-js/react@0.7.22` pin nothing can ever have been stored, so all of this is guaranteed to find nothing. An early return on `supportsClientKey()` (or on "this user has never stored anything") would restore the stated property.

samples.summary: A vitest-importing test-suite file lives in production `src/lib/` rather than under a test path
samples.evidence: `doc-store-contract.ts` opens with `import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"` and its whole body is a `describe` block, but it sits in `packages/frontend/src/lib/` alongside shipped modules and is not named `*.test.ts`, so it is outside the vitest `include` globs in vite.config.ts and reads as production source. Every other frontend suite is either `*.test.ts` or under `tests/`/`__tests__/`. Wrong layer; a `tests/` or `__tests__/` location (or a `.test-support.ts` convention) would keep vitest out of the production source tree. The file's own header explains why it is a transcription of upstream, which is sound reasoning — only its placement is at issue.

samples.summary: Runtime value import of `Client`/`Document`/`Text` from `@yorkie-js/sdk`, which is a devDependency of the frontend
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/package.json` lists `@yorkie-js/sdk` at line 99 under `devDependencies` (only `@yorkie-js/react` is a real dependency, line 66). Before this change, production frontend source imported almost exclusively *types* from the SDK (`collab-document-provider.tsx`, `types/comments.ts`, `types/notes-document.ts`, `wafflebase-doc-store.ts`), with `snapshot-adapters.ts`'s `YSON` as the one value precedent. This change adds runtime class imports — `Client`, `Document`, `Text` in offline-copy-recovery.ts:1 and `Document` in offline-copy.ts:1 — that construct a whole second Yorkie client. It works today because the SDK is a transitive dependency of `@yorkie-js/react`, but relying on a hoisted transitive for shipped runtime code is fragile; the dependency should be declared.

samples.summary: The feature is entirely inert on the shipped dependency pin, so the doc's Goals are unmet on this branch
samples.evidence: `supportsClientKey()` requires `@yorkie-js/react >= 0.7.23`; `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `0.7.22`. Both opt-in entry points are therefore hidden and no document can ever be persisted, so none of the doc's Goals ("edits made while disconnected survive a reload", "the sync chip tells the truth about durability", "work that cannot be reconciled is returned as a document") are observable by any user on this branch. The doc declares this intentional ("PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release... the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), which is why this is minor rather than critical — but it means this change ships a large amount of code whose behavior nothing in CI or in production exercises end-to-end, and a reviewer should confirm the bump is a tracked follow-up rather than an assumption.
searchedFor: read the Rollout section of docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md

samples.summary: Unrelated formatting churn inflates the diff of an already very large change
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/lib/utils.ts` changes only to add semicolons, `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts` is rewritten from double to single quotes throughout with no behavioral change beyond the one new `define` entry, and `packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider.test.tsx` is re-quoted end to end alongside its two substantive mock additions. Prettier is write-only here and no lane checks formatting, so none of this is required; it makes the substantive hunks harder to locate in a diff that is already ~5,000 lines.

samples.summary: Comment on the `saved-locally` icon contradicts the icon it annotates
samples.evidence: The comment reads "Deliberately the same tick as `saved`, not a warning", but the mapped icon on the next line is `IconDeviceDesktop`, not `IconCheck`. The intent (not-an-alarm) still holds, so the code is fine; the comment is stale relative to the icon that was chosen.

mergedFrom.summary: Feature ships entirely unreachable: `@yorkie-js/react` is pinned to `0.7.22` while `MinClientKeyVersion` is `0.7.23`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false, both opt-in entry points are hidden and `useDurableDocument` refuses every document. None of the design's Goals ("edits made while disconnected survive a reload") are observable on this branch. The design doc's Rollout section acknowledges this ("PR 4 lands inert... the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped")

finding.summary: The whole feature is unreachable on the pinned SDK: `@yorkie-js/react` is 0.7.22 while `MinClientKeyVersion` is 0.7.23, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and both opt-in entry points are hidden
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/package.json pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`; yorkie-capabilities.ts sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` and `supportsClientKey()` gates the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx), the chip offer, and `useDurableDocument`'s eligibility. As shipped, no user can opt in, so the design's primary Goal — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload ... on a device where the user has asked for it" — is unreachable on this build. The design anticipates the gate ("Bumping the dependency is the only action needed"), but the Rollout section describes PR 4 as a dark launch "bounded by who turned it on", which presumes somebody can.

verdict.reason: The mechanical facts are accurate (pin 0.7.22 at packages/frontend/package.json:66, MinClientKeyVersion "0.7.23" at yorkie-capabilities.ts:24, gate false, both opt-in surfaces hidden), but the spec-conformance conclusion is contradicted by the spec. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:521-531 states explicitly: "PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release … Nobody on the shipped pin can turn the feature on, which is the safe direction and not the intended one: the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped. Bumping it is the whole remaining action — no code here changes with it — and until then what is being reviewed and tested is the wiring, not the behavior." The same rule is restated at lines 209-213 for the version pin, and the originating task plan repeats it (20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:37-41, 220-221, 242-246: "What is still unreachable, and deliberately: the durable client itself … nothing writes to IndexedDB on this branch"). The reviewer's supporting quote ("dark launch bounded by who turned it on", line 506-508) is answered fifteen lines later in the same section; the design does not presume somebody can opt in on this pin. Additionally the enabling release (yorkie-js-sdk#1357 / react 0.7.23) had not shipped at time of writing per line 523-527, so the bump was not an action available to this change. The inert build is a documented, intentional scope boundary of this PR, not a dropped acceptance criterion — no blocking design-fit violation.
